Interface AtomFactory

All Known Implementing Classes:
DefaultAtomFactory
public interface AtomFactory
Factory for constructing and connecting to Atom instances.

Two creation modes are provided:

  • create(String, Class, T, Duration) (eager) — performs backend I/O immediately to write the initial value and establish the lease. Throws AtomAlreadyExistsException if an atom with the given name already exists. Name collision is the sole trigger — the TTL and initial value passed here are not compared against the pre-existing atom; policy reconciliation is the caller's responsibility.
  • connect(String, Class) — returns an Atom handle without performing backend I/O at factory call time. The first read/write/subscribe operation (Atom.get(), Atom.set(T, Duration), Atom.touch(Duration), or Atom.subscribe()) probes the backend once: if no atom exists at name, that first operation throws AtomNotFoundException. Atom.delete() does not probe and remains a retry-safe no-op when the atom is already gone. Once the one-shot probe passes, subsequent operations behave exactly as they would on a create-sourced handle — terminal-state transitions surface as AtomExpiredException in the normal way.

  • Method Details

    • create

      <T> Atom<T> create(String name, Class<T> type, T initialValue, Duration ttl)
      Creates a new atom with the given name, initial value, and TTL.

      This is an eager operation that immediately writes to the backend. Name collision is the sole trigger for AtomAlreadyExistsException — the initialValue and ttl passed here are not compared against any pre-existing atom's state; policy reconciliation is the caller's responsibility.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the value type
      Parameters:
      name - the unique name for the atom
      type - the value's class
      initialValue - the initial value to store
      ttl - the initial time-to-live for the atom's lease
      Returns:
      a new Atom handle
      Throws:
      AtomAlreadyExistsException - if an atom with name already exists
      IllegalArgumentException - if ttl is zero or negative, or exceeds the maximum allowed duration

    • create

      <T> Atom<T> create(String name, org.jwcarman.codec.TypeRef<T> typeRef, T initialValue, Duration ttl)
      Creates a new atom with the given name, initial value, and TTL, using a TypeRef for generic or complex value types.

      This is an eager operation that immediately writes to the backend. Name collision is the sole trigger for AtomAlreadyExistsException — the initialValue and ttl passed here are not compared against any pre-existing atom's state; policy reconciliation is the caller's responsibility.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the value type
      Parameters:
      name - the unique name for the atom
      typeRef - a type reference describing the value's generic type
      initialValue - the initial value to store
      ttl - the initial time-to-live for the atom's lease
      Returns:
      a new Atom handle
      Throws:
      AtomAlreadyExistsException - if an atom with name already exists
      IllegalArgumentException - if ttl is zero or negative, or exceeds the maximum allowed duration

      <T> Atom<T> connect(String name, Class<T> type)
      Connects to an existing atom by name.

      No backend I/O is performed at factory call time. The first read/write/subscribe operation on the returned handle probes the backend once and throws AtomNotFoundException if no atom exists at name. Atom.delete() does not probe and remains a retry-safe no-op. Once the one-shot probe passes, the handle behaves exactly as one returned from create — subsequent terminal-state transitions surface as AtomExpiredException.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the value type
      Parameters:
      name - the name of the atom to connect to
      type - the value's class
      Returns:
      an Atom handle for the named atom
      Throws:
      AtomNotFoundException - at first operation, if no atom exists at name (surfaced on the first read/write/subscribe call, not at connect time)
